$comment: Machine-readable summary of the Smartlance backend security audit. Contains no keys, tokens, credentials, or PII.

audit.method: source review, empirical probes of security helpers, regression tests, full QA

findings.title: SSRF filter bypass via IPv4-mapped IPv6
findings.behavior: isPrivateOrReservedHostname did not decode IPv4-mapped IPv6, so ::ffff:169.254.169.254 (normalised by the URL parser to ::ffff:a9fe:a9fe) matched no private-range rule.
findings.risk: Server-side requests to loopback, RFC1918 ranges, and the cloud instance metadata endpoint, which can return instance credentials.
findings.evidence: Pre-fix probe: http://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/, http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/, http://[::ffff:10.0.0.1]/ and http://[::]/ all returned ALLOWED.
findings.fix: Decode IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 in both dotted and compressed-hextet form and apply IPv4 private-range rules; block the unspecified address; widen the IPv6 prefix rule.

findings.title: Last-Super-Admin guard is racy
findings.behavior: Active Super Admins were counted outside the write transaction, then the update ran unguarded.
findings.risk: Two concurrent demote or disable requests with exactly two Super Admins both pass the guard, leaving zero active Super Admins and an unrecoverable admin lockout, since manage_users is exclusive to SUPER_ADMIN.
findings.evidence: Standalone count() followed by an unrelated update() with no isolation between them.
findings.fix: Count and update now run inside prisma.$transaction at Serializable isolation so Postgres aborts the losing transaction.

findings.title: Slug rename-back takes a published page offline
findings.behavior: upsertSlugRedirect had no self-redirect check and no awareness of existing rows, unlike manual redirects which run detectRedirectLoop.
findings.risk: Renaming a published entity a -> b -> a leaves /a redirecting to /b while the entity lives at /a. The proxy applies DB redirects before rendering, producing an infinite 301 loop that removes a live indexed page from the site.
findings.evidence: proxy.ts applies applyDbSlugRedirect ahead of NextResponse.next(); findActiveRedirect matches sourcePath with status ACTIVE.
findings.fix: Skip self-redirects, disable any ACTIVE redirect whose source equals the new live destination, and repoint redirects that targeted the old path so chains collapse.

findings.title: AI content-assistant actions skipped the same-origin check
findings.behavior: Four mutating Server Actions called requireAdminUser but not assertSameOrigin, unlike the other ten action modules.
findings.risk: Defence-in-depth gap. Next.js applies its own Server Action origin check, but if that were misconfigured a logged-in editor could be induced to burn AI budget or apply a proposal.
findings.evidence: Coverage scan: ai-content-assistant-actions.ts had 4 exported actions and 0 assertSameOrigin calls.
findings.fix: assertSameOrigin() added to all four actions; coverage is now uniform across all 11 modules.

findings.title: Six outbound calls had no timeout
findings.behavior: Webhook, Resend, IndexNow, Tavily, GNews and NewsAPI fetches passed no signal or only an optional caller signal that callers omitted.
findings.risk: A hung upstream holds the serverless function open until the platform kills it, turning a slow provider into a failed-looking request.
findings.evidence: Exhaustive fetch inventory; LLM adapters (90s) and safeFetchText (12s) were already bounded.
findings.fix: Added lib/ops/request-timeout.ts with named budgets (notification 10s, indexing 8s, research 15s) composed with any caller signal, applied to all six.

findings.title: Login timing revealed account existence; throttling keyed only on email
findings.behavior: Unknown or disabled accounts returned before any Argon2 work while valid accounts paid full verification cost. Rate limiting used the submitted email only.
findings.risk: Admin email enumeration by response timing, and unbounded credential stuffing across many accounts from one source.
findings.evidence: Early return at the unknown-user branch preceded verifyPassword; isLoginRateLimited was called with the email alone.
findings.fix: burnPasswordVerification performs a real Argon2 verification against a throwaway hash on the rejection path; a per-source-address limit (30 per 15 min) now runs alongside the per-account limit (10 per 15 min).

findings.title: AI proposal decisions were unvalidated client JSON
findings.behavior: JSON.parse(decisionsJson) was cast directly to FieldDecision[] with no runtime validation.
findings.risk: Low. The downstream field allowlist is the real control and held. The unbounded array and unchecked shape broke the runtime-validation boundary maintained elsewhere, and a non-array body threw a raw TypeError.
findings.evidence: Direct cast with no schema; array length unbounded.
findings.fix: Zod envelope: max 200 entries, field constrained to a 1-120 character string, decision restricted to accept|keep|edit. editedValue stays unknown by design, since editors may hand-write any value for an allowlisted field.

findings.title: Media list endpoint accepted unvalidated enums and pagination
findings.behavior: status was cast as MediaAssetStatus with no check; pagination relied on downstream clamping.
findings.risk: Invalid enum values reached Prisma and produced unhandled 500s instead of a clean 400.
findings.evidence: Direct `as` cast on a query parameter.
findings.fix: Zod schema at the boundary with enums derived from the generated Prisma enum objects so they cannot drift from the schema, plus explicit page and pageSize bounds.

findings.title: Unpatched image-size advisory was reachable through HEIF
findings.behavior: The magic-byte sniffer treated the generic HEIF major brand mif1 as AVIF, so a crafted HEIF file passed validation and reached imageSize().
findings.risk: Denial of service via the unfixed infinite-loop advisories GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr and GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq. An infinite loop is not recoverable by the surrounding try/catch. Requires an authenticated admin with manage_media. ICNS and JXL were never reachable, being rejected by sniffing.
findings.evidence: npm audit reports 1 high severity with no fix available; sniffMime accepted mif1 as image/avif.
findings.fix: Only the true AVIF major brands avif and avis are accepted. This also corrects a MIME-labelling bug that stored HEIF files as image/avif.

findings.title: Node 24 reinterprets sslmode=require as verify-full
findings.behavior: The build emits a runtime warning that prefer, require and verify-ca are treated as aliases for verify-full. Both connection strings use sslmode=require.
findings.risk: None currently. verify-full is the stricter interpretation and Neon presents publicly trusted certificates, so verification succeeds. A future move to a host using self-signed or private-CA certificates would fail with the same connection string that works today.
findings.evidence: Build output warning on Node v24.13.1; connections succeeded throughout build and test run.
findings.fix: None applied. Setting sslmode=verify-full explicitly would document the effective behavior and silence the warning.

acceptedRisks.title: Publishing is not transactional
acceptedRisks.detail: Status promotion, revision creation and audit write are sequential across roughly eight repositories. Published state is a single row update and stays coherent; only bookkeeping can be incomplete. Fixing it warrants its own reviewed change.

acceptedRisks.title: Rate limiting is per-instance and in memory
acceptedRisks.detail: Deliberate, to avoid introducing Redis. Effective limit is roughly configured_limit x instance_count on serverless. Front with CDN rate limiting if stronger guarantees are required.

acceptedRisks.title: DNS rebinding is not blocked
acceptedRisks.detail: Hostnames are validated on the initial URL and every redirect hop, but resolved IPs are not pinned for the connection. Closing this requires resolve-then-connect control the fetch API does not expose.

acceptedRisks.title: X-Forwarded-For is trusted for rate-limit bucketing
acceptedRisks.detail: The header is not authenticated, so spoofing moves an attacker between buckets. It cannot bypass the per-account login limit.

acceptedRisks.title: Draft saves demote published content without revalidating
acceptedRisks.detail: For most content families a draft save sets status DRAFT without revalidating the public path, so the CDN may serve a stale page. Pre-existing CMS semantic and a product decision, not a security issue.

acceptedRisks.title: Unbounded AI context reads
acceptedRisks.detail: lib/ai/knowledge.ts and lib/ai/topic-intelligence/content-index.ts load every published entity with no take. Prompt output is capped downstream. Acceptable at current catalogue size.

manualActions: Take a database backup and perform a restore drill
Confirm ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET is at least 32 random characters in production
Set AI_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY explicitly so session-secret rotation does not destroy provider keys
Verify the object storage bucket is not publicly listable
Confirm MEDIA_STORAGE_PROVIDER=s3 and that S3 credentials work
Verify SPF and DKIM for the configured email sender domain
Decide whether per-instance rate limiting is sufficient; add CDN rate limiting if not
Add error alerting so provider and publish failures are noticed
Track image-size for a patched release and upgrade when available
Review hosting execution limits against long AI research runs

qa.lintNote: All pre-existing React set-state-in-effect issues in admin client components; untouched by this audit
qa.npmAuditNote: image-size, no upstream fix available; reachability mitigated in BE-09
